newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea wet crude firm on good demand, paper mixed.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea wet crude firm on good demand, paper mixed.

text.p: North Sea wet crudes traded firmer amid active demand on Wednesday while paper was mixed and outright values slid, traders said.
"North Sea is picking up quite well," one wet trader said.
Spot market sentiment was supported by good demand for early July cargoes and smaller than anticipated loading programmes for the main North Sea export systems.

Iraq news also lent support, with an Iraqi diplomat declaring Baghdad would not resume oil exports under the second phase of the U.N. "oil-for-food" programme until it had spent all the money earned from the first phase.
The unspent aid money stands at around $800 million.
In addition, two cargoes from Norway's Oseberg system equivalent to about 1.1 million barrels have been cancelled from the July programme, a trader said.
A Flotta loading July 15-17 moved at a 65 cent discount to international benchmark Dated Brent, around 20 cents firmer than last assessed.
An Ekofisk loading July 6-9 moved at Dated Brent +10 cents, while another loading June 5-7 changed hands at Dated +18 cents, well up from the last traded level of Dated -5 cents.
An Oseberg loading July 4-6 moved at Dated +10 cents, well above the level of a Monday trade at Dated evens.
One Forties cargo was offered at Dated +30 cents and bid at +20 while another was heard sold but no details were available.
One Statfjord was heard done, possibly as high as Dated +40 cents but there were no details.
"The market looks balanced. Sellers aren't panicking but neither are buyers," said one crude trader.

Paper was mixed. Brent Contracts for Difference for next week traded twice in the afternoon at August Brent -32 cents. The following week (June 30-July 4) was offered at August -32 cents but no bid was heard. The next week (July 7-11) was talked at August -35/-31 cents.
In intermonth spreads, July/August was slightly firmer at -17/-14 cents. August/September was weaker at -18/-16.
The front month August Brent IPE contract was down 35 cents at $17.73 a barrel at 1755 GMT.
The two Brent crude cargoes in Wednesday's paper chains were kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline by Stasco, traders said.
